name: four.meme
rootCause: BNB-based memecoin launchpad Four.Meme was attacked. According to the SlowMist security team’s analysis, the attacker purchased a small amount of tokens before launch through the 0x7f79f6df function of Four.Meme, and used this feature to send tokens to a specified PancakeSwap Pair address that had not yet been created. This allowed the attacker to create the Pair and add liquidity without needing to transfer the yet-to-be-launched tokens to the Pair, bypassing the transfer restrictions (MODE_TRANSFER_RESTRICTED) that applied before the Four.Meme Token launch. Ultimately, the attacker was able to add liquidity at an unintended price to steal pool liquidity.

descriptions.text: BNB-based memecoin launchpad Four.Meme was attacked. According to the SlowMist security team’s analysis, the attacker purchased a small amount of tokens before launch through the 0x7f79f6df function of Four.Meme, and used this feature to send tokens to a specified PancakeSwap Pair address that had not yet been created. This allowed the attacker to create the Pair and add liquidity without needing to transfer the yet-to-be-launched tokens to the Pair, bypassing the transfer restrictions (MODE_TRANSFER_RESTRICTED) that applied before the Four.Meme Token launch. Ultimately, the attacker was able to add liquidity at an unintended price to steal pool liquidity.

Four Meme's launchpad on BNB Chain was exploited on March 18, 2025 for around $120,000. The attacker bypassed intended transfer restrictions, sent pre-launch tokens to a liquidity pool, and manipulated the launch to drain funds. The technical root cause is a failure to enforce pre-launch transfer locks on the token contract. The Four Meme token's transfer function did not enforce the intended pre-launch restriction. This allowed direct transfers of pre-launch tokens,including to the predicted PancakeSwap pair address,allowing the attacker to manipulate liquidity before official trading began.
